header.running_head: Relationships between Men, Women and Children

blocks.text: enter. Yet again the slave went in and emerged saying, 'I mentioned your name to him but he merely remained silent.' As I turned to leave, the slave suddenly called for me saying, 'You may enter, for Rasulullaah ﷺ has granted you permission.' When I entered, I found Rasulullaah ﷺ reclining against a straw mat that had left imprints on his side. 'Have you divorced your wives, O Rasulullaah ﷺ?' I asked. Raising his head, he replied, 'No.' 'Allaahu Akbar!' I cried out. I then said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You have seen that we the members of the Quraysh always had the upper hand over our wives. When we arrived in Madinah, we encountered people (the Ansaar) whose women had the upper hand over them. Our women then started learning from their women. When I became angry with my wife one day (and told her something), she surprised me by back chatting. When I objected to her back chatting, she said, 'What are you objecting about my back chatting when I can swear by Allaah that the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ backchat to him? In fact some of them (when angry) shun him morning to evening. I said, 'Whichever of them does that is at a loss and destroyed! Does any of them not fear that Allaah would be angry with her because His Rasool ﷺ is angry with her? She will then most certainly be destroyed.' This made Rasulullaah ﷺ smile.

'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I continued, 'I then went to Hafsah and told her, 'Never be deceived by the fact that your companion (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)) is prettier than you and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ.' Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled again. Then I asked, 'Should I continue with this light-hearted talk?' 'By all means,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said. I then sat down and I swear by Allaah that when I looked about the room, all I saw was three pieces of undyed leather. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I said, 'Pray to Allaah to grant an abundance of wealth to your Ummah. Allaah has given abundance to the Romans and Persians even though they do not worship Him (so he will readily give us as well).'

Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat up straight and said, 'Are you also in doubt, O son of Khattaab? They are people whose rewards (for their good deeds) have been brought forward to this world (without any share left for the Aakhirah).' I then quickly said, 'Do seek forgiveness for me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ.' Because he was so angry with them at the time, Rasulullaah ﷺ had vowed not to go to his wives for an entire month until Allaah directed him otherwise." [^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ separated from his wives, I entered the Masjid where I saw the people fondling pebbles as they said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' This incident took place before the injunction of Hijaab was ordained. I said to myself, 'I am going to find out properly what is happening (whether Rasulullaah ﷺ had divorced them or not).'" The Hadith continues to mention how Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to both Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) as well as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to admonish them.
